findings.description: The header comment added at the soft-source site says the planner 'fails closed (every hop agy-checked) if the lib did not load', but _adv_agy_filter_chain does the opposite: when _adv_agy_lib returns false it logs a WARN and returns the chain unfiltered, so a gemini-headless hop stays planned. Before this diff the inline reader filtered the literal gemini-headless hop with no library dependency, so a consumer checkout where .claude/scripts/lib/agy-gate-lib.sh is missing or stale (the soft `source ... 2>/dev/null || true` exists precisely to tolerate that) now regresses from 'planned: false, reason: opt_in_required' to 'planned, then refused/skipped by cheval'. Additionally, agy_gate_warn_once is invoked inside _adv_agy_filter_chain, which main calls under $(...), against the lib's own contract that the once-flag is a shell variable and must not be set from a subshell; it is only quiet today because main calls it at top level first.
findings.failure_mode: With the lib absent, the companion chain keeps the agy hop; the dissent envelope records that voice as a cheval refusal/skip instead of opt_in_required, and the top-of-file comment misleads the next maintainer into assuming fail-closed planning.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a minimal inline fallback in _adv_agy_filter_chain for the lib-missing path (drop hops whose raw or canonical id matches gemini-headless|*:gemini-headless|gemini-headless:*), and correct the header comment. Remove the agy_gate_warn_once call from inside _adv_agy_filter_chain and rely on the top-level call in main.

findings.description: The flavor fallback is selected by output shape, not by yq flavor: if the typed go-yq expression yields anything other than the literal 'true'/'false', the function re-runs `yq '.hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in == true'`. That untyped comparison is only a typed test under python yq (jq semantics). Under mikefarah go yq, `==` on two scalars compares node values as strings, so a quoted string "true" compares equal to boolean true. Today go yq cannot realistically reach the fallback (the first expression always prints true/false for any node), so there is no live exposure, but the library's single stated invariant — a string "true" never opts in — now rests on an incidental property of the first expression rather than on the branch guard.
findings.failure_mode: If a future go-yq version changes the output of the tag-test expression (e.g. multi-line or styled output), the fallback runs under go yq and `agy_opt_in: "true"` silently opts the planner into the agy route, defeating the gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Select the fallback by detecting the python flavor explicitly (e.g. `yq --version 2>&1 | grep -qi jq` or the absence of 'mikefarah'/'v4'), or restrict the fallback to only run when the first call exited non-zero AND the flavor is python. Alternatively make the python branch typed too: `(.hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in | type) == "boolean" and .hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in == true`.

findings.cross_file_justification: routes_to_agy is introduced in the diff and is consumed by run-preflight.sh P3 (also diff-touched: the source line). P3 uses the predicate only on the gated branch; with the opt-in on it falls through to a usability check that does not know the voice is agy-routed.
findings.description: P3 calls routes_to_agy "$m" "$p3_mode" only when p3_agy_on is 0. When the opt-in is true and mode is cli-only, a Google API model such as gemini-2.5-pro (or google:gemini-*) is agy-routed per the shared predicate, but cli_for returns "" for it, so usability is decided by cred_present google (GOOGLE_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY) rather than by `agy` being on PATH. P3 can therefore report PASS for a stage whose only voice cannot run on this host, and STAGE_ONLY/P4 will attribute it to the google provider's API breaker rather than the headless one.
findings.failure_mode: Preflight passes, the run starts, and the stage's voice fails at dispatch with PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE (agy binary absent) — the exact 'planned voice that cannot exist' G-1 is meant to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: After computing cli, add: `if routes_to_agy "$m" "$p3_mode"; then cli=agy; fi` so the agy-routed voice is judged by `command -v agy` like the other *-headless hops, and label it `(cli agy)` in usable_names/missing.
